h: Repton, Railway Paths and a Slower Pace
p: There's a lot to be said for a day out where nothing beeps, flashes or needs charging. A visit to meet the Redwings horses is exactly that: a gentle, slow wander where the best moment might be a donkey resting its chin on the fence while you scratch behind its ears. It's ideal for families who need a reset after a hectic week, and for anyone who's a bit nervous around animals and wants to build confidence in calm surroundings.

Make it easy on yourself by keeping the visit simple. Wellies or walking boots, a waterproof and a flask cover most eventualities. Listen out for any talks or meet-and-greet moments with staff, as that's when you'll learn the real stories of how individual horses came into the charity's care, and those stories tend to stick with kids far longer than any sign. Remember the residents are rescued animals first and foremost, so follow the guidance about touching and never offer them your own snacks.

Aylsham has some surprising history tucked into its streets. Humphry Repton, the famous landscape gardener who shaped grand estates up and down the country, is buried in the churchyard of St Michael's in the market place, a fitting resting place for a man who spent his life designing gardens. The town also sits on Marriott's Way, a long walking and cycling trail along an old railway line that runs towards Norwich, perfect for a flat, traffic-free ride if you've brought the bikes. The weekly market and the old coaching inns round the market place add to the easy-going, proper Norfolk feel.
